project_specification.project_name: nullius — Telegram alerting for the scheduled BingX VST bot
project_specification.addition_summary: Extend the router workspace member (packages/router, import name router) so the unattended Stage 2 bot on the BingX VST sub-account nullius01 reports to its operator through a Telegram bot. Today a systemd user timer runs one rebalance slot every 4 hours (`./run.sh vst-rebalance`). A daily-loss halt, a refused leg, a crashed slot or a dead timer shows up only in journalctl. This addition sends Telegram messages: - urgent on a daily-loss halt; - a warning when a slot exits with a refused leg; - a silent summary after every slot; - an urgent alert when a slot cannot run at all (systemd OnFailure); - an urgent alert when no slot has finished for 5 hours (an hourly heartbeat timer). Alerting is best-effort by design. A Telegram failure is logged and never changes a slot's outcome, its orders or its exit code.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / SQLite stores addressed by DATABASE_URL / pytest (ruff conventions) / systemd user units under deploy/systemd/
existing_context.test_baseline: workspace suite tests/ (1573) and packages/router/tests (1296) passing on main
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses, stdlib-first (no third-party dependency), typed refusals that open with a greppable code word and are defined in the raising module, subclassing router.errors.RouterError (router.errors and router/__init__.py are not edited). Follow CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section. Tests never reach the network; HTTP goes through an injected transport. Existing pieces: - router.bingx_rebalance.main(argv, …, now=, emit=) runs one slot and emits one JSON summary line (slot, rebalance_ts, opening_equity, current_equity, daily_loss, daily_loss_limit, cancelled, reconciled, orders, refused, skipped, exit_code). It returns exit 0 when all orders are placed or prior, 1 on a refused leg, and 3 on a daily-loss refusal (daily_loss_halt or orders_halted). - deploy/systemd/nullius-vst-rebalance.service is a oneshot with SuccessExitStatus=0 1 3. It runs `run.sh vst-rebalance`, with PATH set and OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN loaded from %h/.config/op/service-token. - run.sh already routes `./run.sh vst-alert` to python -m router.bingx_alert and `./run.sh vst-heartbeat` to python -m router.bingx_heartbeat, under op run with .env.vst.tpl and DATABASE_URL defaulting to ~/.local/share/nullius/vst.db. The operator adds TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID to .env.vst.tpl (1Password references); that is not part of this spec. Telegram Bot API facts: POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage with chat_id, text, optional parse_mode and disable_notification. The response is {"ok": true, "result": {...}}, or {"ok": false, "error_code": n, "description": "..."} on failure. The token is part of the URL path, so any URL in an error message carries the secret.

category.name: Telegram Alerting
category.feature: System sends one Telegram alert with a level of urgent, warning or info through POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage, using TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID. - The message opens with the level and "nullius VST". - An info alert is sent with disable_notification true. - It reaches only api.telegram.org through a host guard, and returns True when Telegram answers ok. - On a missing variable, a transport error, a timeout of 10 seconds or an ok:false answer, it returns False and logs one line naming the failure. The token never appears in that line, a repr, an exception or stdout: the bot path is scrubbed from every URL. - `python -m router.bingx_alert --test` sends an info test message and exits 0 on delivery, 1 otherwise. - `python -m router.bingx_alert --unit NAME --event failure` sends an urgent "slot could not run" alert naming the unit and the journalctl command to read it.

System alerts on every rebalance slot's outcome without changing it. After each slot it records the slot's completion (book_id, slot, finished_at, exit_code) in its own table in the DATABASE_URL store, then sends feature 1's alert: - urgent for exit 3, naming the daily loss, the limit and the manual reset; - warning for exit 1, listing each refused symbol with its code and message; - info for exit 0, summarising the orders placed, prior and skipped, the orders cancelled, whether the previous slot was reconciled, and the day's loss. The JSON summary line, the exit code and every order are identical whether alerting succeeds, fails or is unconfigured. An alert that raises is caught and logged.

System checks the bot's heartbeat from `python -m router.bingx_heartbeat --max-age-hours 5`. It reads the newest slot completion that feature 2 recorded. When there is none, or the newest is older than the limit, it sends an urgent alert naming the last slot and its age, and exits 1. Otherwise it sends nothing and exits 0. At most one heartbeat alert is sent per stale slot, so an hourly check does not repeat it every hour. deploy/systemd/ holds a oneshot heartbeat service, with the same environment as the rebalance service (PATH, and the token loaded from %h/.config/op/service-token), that runs `run.sh vst-heartbeat --max-age-hours 5`, and a timer that fires it hourly at minute 35 with Persistent=true.

System sends an urgent Telegram alert when a scheduled slot cannot run at all (the systemd unit fails). The rebalance service gains OnFailure=nullius-vst-alert@%n.service. The template unit nullius-vst-alert@.service is a oneshot, with the same PATH and token loading as the rebalance service, that runs `run.sh vst-alert --unit %i --event failure`. Exit codes 1 and 3 stay successes, since feature 2 alerts on those. Tests parse the units and pin the OnFailure line, the template's ExecStart, the PATH entry, the token-file load and the absence of any literal token. One test runs the template's expanded ExecStart under env -i with run.sh stubbed, to prove PATH and the token reach the child.

project_specification.integration_points: New modules router.bingx_alert and router.bingx_heartbeat are both runnable with python -m. Their tests, plus tests/test_bingx_alert_units.py for the units, sit in packages/router/tests/. The new units sit in deploy/systemd/. Every new file is committed as an empty stub so its claim resolves. bingx_rebalance gains the slot-completion table and the alert call at the end of a slot, after the summary line is emitted. Nothing installs, enables or reloads units; that is an operator step.
project_specification.constraints: - The Telegram token never appears in any repository file, test fixture, log line, exception message, repr or stdout. Tests use a fake token and assert it is absent from every captured output. - Alerting never alters trading: a slot's orders, summary line and exit code are the same with alerting up, down or unconfigured. - No test opens a network connection, reads 1Password or a real credential, or edits .env.tpl, .env.vst.tpl, run.sh, claw-forge.yaml or claw-forge.local.yaml. - No third-party dependency; pyproject.toml and uv.lock are not edited. - Stage 1 and Stage 2 modules other than bingx_rebalance keep their behaviour, and their tests stay green unchanged. - Nothing installs, enables or reloads systemd units. - Do not edit docs/user-journeys/. - All existing workspace and member tests must stay green.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 2: slot alerts with the completion record (feature 2), and the OnFailure template (feature 4).
Phase 3: the heartbeat check and its timer (feature 3).
